claims.text: Controls shine for up to 8 hours

cautions: Stop using it if you get stinging, burning or redness that does not fade.
Keep the rest of your routine the same on both halves, and scan at the same time and in the same light each day.
plan.summary: Put the gel on one half of your face and nothing on the other for 28 days, scanning once a day. Oiliness and dryness can change within a day or two. Pores need weeks, so early pore results are too early to tell. One scan a day costs 9 units, well within today's 150.

decision.message: Your first scan with the gel already shows less oiliness and a little less dryness on the treated side. It is a single reading taken right after starting, so it is too early to tell if that lasts, and pores need weeks to show anything. Keep your routine the same on both halves and scan again tomorrow at the same time and in the same light.

verdict.headline: Day 0: first scan is in. Oiliness and dryness look better on the treated side, but this is a single scan, so it is too early to judge the product's claims.

concerns.text: Treated side reads 2.6 and control reads 10.5. The treated side started oilier (12.8 vs 10.0). The effect is about 10.8 points better than that starting gap, well past the 1.25 threshold. This is one scan at hour 0, so it shows the first reading, not how long it lasts.
No difference yet. Both sides read 0.0 before and after. Pores change over weeks, so too early to tell.

Treated side went from 48.9 to 46.8 while the control stayed about the same (46.2 to 46.5). That is 2.4 points better than the starting gap, past the 1.25 threshold. It is one scan, so keep watching before trusting it.
